verification.summary: The previous blocker (comment-added log line never checked) is now fixed, but the tracker sweep step only guards against double-touching and checks the first issue's count — it never asserts that any issue besides the first actually received the tracker's comment, so a tracker that does nothing to everyone else would still pass.

mustFix.problem: Step 7 checks FIRST_FINAL_COUNT==2 and that no issue has more than one tracker comment, but it never checks that issues other than the first (present before the tracker ran) actually gained a 'GitHub Issues Tracker' comment. accs.md expects 'the rest should have 1' with 0 only tolerated for late-loaded entries — as written, a tracker that silently does nothing for every issue but the first would still pass.

shouldFix.quote: for(const b of blocks) console.log('n='+b.n+' ids='+b.ids.length+' trunc='+b.truncated);
shouldFix.problem: scan_snapshots computes line counts and a truncated flag per block but accs.bash never asserts on them, so the buffer-cap-vs-truncation behaviour stays completely untested even though the contract describes it in detail.

shouldKnow.quote: # spec 001 script has already exited on its own; nothing more to terminate.
shouldKnow.problem: accs.md says to 'terminate' spec 001's script on success, but this implementation just runs it synchronously and assumes it self-exits/self-cleans; reasonable, but it's an undocumented assumption about spec 001's accs.bash shape that should be flagged in Assumptions Taken.
